results.title: Valenzuela gov't adopts one-ID policy for city transactions
results.description: Valenzuela City residents are now required to present only one valid government-issued identification card (ID) for transactions requiring identity verification at city government offices. Mayor Weslie “Wes” Gatchalian signed Executive Order No. 2026-151 on Nov. 9 to simplify government transactions and reduce processing time for residents. The policy applies to both in-person and online transactions with city government offices where identity verification is required. Under the order, residents may present one valid government-issued ID in physical or electronic format, provided it bears their photograph and signature. "Where identity verification is required by law or the applicable Citizen's Charter, the office shall accept one (1) valid government-issued ID under the subsequent sections," Section 1 of the executive order states. Accepted IDs include the Philippine National ID, passport, driver's license, Professional Regulation Commission ID, Integrated Bar of the Philippines ID, National Bureau of Investigation clearance, police clearance, postal ID, and voter's ID or certification. Other accepted documents include the Government Service Insurance System e-card, Social Security System card, PhilHealth ID, senior citizen ID or booklet, Overseas Workers Welfare Administration ID, Overseas Filipino Worker ID, seaman's book, and alien certificate of registration. Government office IDs, persons with disability IDs or booklets, Department of Social Welfare and Development certifications, solo parent IDs, Tax Identification Number IDs, Unified Multi-Purpose ID cards, and residency IDs issued by local government units are also recognized. However, city government offices may still request additional identification when required by law or when discrepancies or concerns about an ID's authenticity cannot be resolved. In such cases, residents must first be given a chance to explain the discrepancy or present another valid ID. Any request for additional identification must also be approved by the concerned office head or an authorized supervisor. The order also requires city government offices to protect residents' personal information during identity verification. "Offices shall inspect or authenticate the ID and process only the personal data necessary for the transaction," Section 4 states. The provision also requires compliance with Republic Act No. 10173, or the Data Privacy Act of 2012, when collecting, copying, or retaining identification information. The executive order took effect immediately upon its issuance on Nov. 9. The city government said the policy aims to remove unnecessary documentary requirements and make public services faster and more convenient for residents.
